A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete versions of the same survey. Their text, equations, figures and seven tables support reliable comparison. Neither contains a separate appendix; both end with references.

before.justification: v2.pdf surveys published methods and evaluation practices. Its tables and illustrations summarize cited work; no original experimental, simulation, user-study or empirical data-analysis results are reported.

after.justification: v3.pdf remains a literature survey. The added timeline and expanded mapping diagram organize existing work without introducing original empirical results.

M1.justification: Neither version proposes an original algorithm. The dense-geometric pipeline added to v3 Figure 7 illustrates mapping concepts already discussed in v2; it does not establish a method revision.

E1.justification: The datasets and tasks catalogued in Tables 3–6 remain the same. Neither version conducts training or evaluation, and the new timeline introduces no tested scenario.

E2.justification: The tables retain the same surveyed methods. These are descriptive literature comparisons, and no experimentally evaluated baseline is added, removed or replaced.

E3.justification: Section 6 and Table 7 retain the same evaluation metrics and practices. Settings described for surveyed methods are unchanged, and neither version introduces an original experimental protocol.

E4.justification: No ablation, sensitivity test, robustness experiment or empirical case study is added or removed. The existing robustness discussion and supplementary examples are retained.

E5.justification: The discussion of uncertainty in mapping remains unchanged. Neither version reports original repeated runs, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: The summary tables and cited empirical findings remain unchanged in substance. Updated years for ConceptGraphs, GaussNav and OneMap are publication metadata, not revised performance results.

T1.justification: The SLAM equations (1–5), projection equations (6–7), and mathematical descriptions of map structures and aggregation are unchanged. The added diagrams introduce no formal assumptions, derivations or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same taxonomy, survey scope and central claims about open-vocabulary mapping, representation trade-offs and future research needs.

C2.justification: The interpretations and limitations concerning efficiency, scalability, sensor noise, dynamic environments and evaluation gaps remain unchanged. The timeline reiterates the existing interpretation of a shift toward open-vocabulary maps.

D1.justification: The bibliography adds repository and project access information for surveyed work, including a BEVBert repository URL and a MOPA project URL. Implementation settings and experimental reproducibility details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 4.3.1 drops Clio from examples of task-agnostic point-cloud mapping, while retaining it among topological/open-vocabulary methods elsewhere. Broader positioning remains stable; publication updates and merged duplicate references do not introduce distinct new works.

P1.justification: Edits include more consistent grid-map terminology, expanded figure captions, revised acknowledgements, and bibliography standardization and deduplication. The section organization and almost all substantive prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v3 adds a historical timeline as Figure 6 and redraws v2 Figure 6 as Figure 7, adding a dense-geometric pipeline and rearranging explanatory insets. Existing figures and tables are retained with limited relabeling, relocation and page reflow.

improvement.justification: The expanded mapping schematic, reference cleanup and added access links modestly improve explanation and usability. The new timeline has a localized inconsistency: Topo SLAM appears before 2001 although Table 4 dates it to 2001. The presentation and source-tracing gains outweigh this small issue, while the scientific synthesis remains essentially unchanged.
